recipes.title: Lemon salmon and asparagus
recipes.summary: Lemon salmon with asparagus and garlic.

ingredients.name: Skin-on salmon fillets
ingredients.state: raw, thawed; individual fillets about 1 inch thick
ingredients.note: Choose individual fillets about 170 g (6 oz) each, keeping the stated thickness.

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.note: Half to asparagus; half to salmon.

ingredients.name: Garlic powder
ingredients.note: Divide equally.

ingredients.name: Fine salt
ingredients.note: Use the proportional split described in the method.

ingredients.name: Lemon zest
ingredients.note: Use finely grated zest.

ingredients.name: Hemp hearts
ingredients.note: Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Preheat both fryers to 390°F. Toss asparagus with half the oil, half the garlic, and half the salt. Spread in one basket without a dense pile.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pat salmon dry. Rub with remaining oil, garlic, salt, pepper, and zest. Put skin-side down in the other basket with gaps between fillets. Start both together.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Check asparagus at 7 minutes; medium stalks usually need 7–10. Check salmon at 10 minutes; allow 10–14 to reach 145°F. Remove each when ready. Finish with lemon juice and hemp.

equipment: Two air fryers with room for four fillets in one basket and 454 g asparagus in the other

timeline.attention: Toss and load separate baskets; preheat overlaps prep.

Check fish at 145°F; add lemon and hemp.

tips: Thin asparagus needs an earlier check.
Keep the fillets skin-side down and apart.
recipes.fallback: If either basket cannot hold its full batch, use two half-sheet pans at 425°F: fish about 12–18 min, asparagus 10–15 min; allow 25–35 min total.
limitations: Basket fit and actual thickness can change the time; first cook has not been kitchen-tested.

recipes.title: Smoky chicken thighs and broccoli
recipes.summary: Smoky chicken thighs with roasted broccoli.

ingredients.name: Boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.state: raw, thawed, unfolded; no more than ¾ inch thick

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.note: Half to broccoli; half to chicken.

ingredients.name: Fine salt
ingredients.note: Use the proportional split described in the method.

ingredients.name: Nutritional yeast
ingredients.note: Add after cooking.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Preheat both fryers to 390°F. Toss broccoli with half the oil and one third of the salt; load one basket without crowding. In a separate bowl coat chicken with the remaining oil and salt, paprika, garlic, oregano, and pepper.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Put unfolded thighs smooth-side up in the other basket without overlapping. Start chicken. Five minutes later, start broccoli.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Shake broccoli once halfway through its 10–14-minute cook. Chicken usually needs 16–22 minutes; check the thickest pieces for 165°F. No chicken flip is required, though the underside browns less. Finish broccoli with lemon and nutritional yeast. Broccoli is ready when stems are fork-tender and crowns are lightly browned; time alone is not its endpoint.

equipment: Two air fryers with uncrowded baskets
Separate raw-poultry bowl and clean serving tools

timeline.attention: Start chicken first; preheat overlaps prep.
Load broccoli basket.
Shake broccoli once halfway; check chicken thickest pieces for 165°F.
Add lemon and yeast after cooking.

tips: Chicken underside browns less without a flip.
Keep yeast out of the fryer to avoid scorching.
recipes.fallback: If baskets cannot hold the batch, use two oven pans at 425°F for about 20–25 min; allow 35–40 min total and check chicken for 165°F.
limitations: Smaller fryer baskets require the oven fallback or extra batches.

recipes.title: Pesto cod and zucchini
recipes.summary: Pesto cod with zucchini.

ingredients.name: Cod fillets
ingredients.state: raw, thawed; individual fillets about 1 inch thick
ingredients.note: Choose individual fillets about 170 g (6 oz) each, keeping the stated thickness.

ingredients.name: DeLallo basil pesto
ingredients.note: Weigh the scaled amount; do not infer tablespoons from the unusual label volume. Substitute at most 2 g net carbs per 30 g.

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.note: Three quarters to zucchini; remainder to fish.

ingredients.name: Fine salt
ingredients.note: Use the measured salt in the zucchini seasoning.

ingredients.name: Hemp hearts
ingredients.note: Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss zucchini with three quarters of the oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on one half-sheet pan. Pat fish dry, rub with the remaining oil, and place on the other pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Start the zucchini pan first. After 6 minutes, add the fish pan. Check zucchini from 18 minutes of its own cooking time for browned edges and a tender center; allow about 18–23 minutes. Check fish after 12 minutes of its own cooking time; allow about 12–18 minutes to reach 145°F. Remove each pan at its endpoint and serve promptly. If either needs longer, keep checking; do not overcook the fish to match the vegetables.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Spoon pesto over cooked fish. Finish fish and zucchini with lemon and hemp. Applying pesto after cooking keeps its basil flavor and avoids burning the sauce.

timeline.attention: Preheat overlaps prep; fish and zucchini get separate pans.
Add fish pan after 6 minutes: one scheduled main-appliance action.

recipes.title: Spinach, feta, and hemp frittata
recipes.summary: Spinach, feta and hemp frittata with salad.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.note: Mix into the eggs.

ingredients.name: Frozen chopped spinach
ingredients.state: package weight before thawing and squeezing
ingredients.note: Heat according to package directions, cool until safe to handle and press very dry in a sieve.

ingredients.note: Cheese label and rennet vary.

ingredients.name: Hemp hearts
ingredients.note: Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

ingredients.name: Nutritional yeast
ingredients.note: Mix into eggs.

ingredients.name: Fine salt
ingredients.note: Use the measured salt in the egg mixture; feta adds salt too.

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.note: One quarter for dish; three quarters for salad. Base batch is 1 tsp + 1 tbsp.

ingredients.name: Salad greens
ingredients.note: Buy by scaled edible weight.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Heat spinach in the microwave according to its package during preheating, then let it cool until safe to handle and press very dry in a fine-mesh sieve with a spoon. Do not squeeze hot spinach with bare hands. Use one quarter of the oil to grease one 9-inch square metal dish for two or four servings, or two matching dishes for six or eight; each must be at least 2 inches deep.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Whisk eggs, water, garlic, salt, and pepper. Stir in squeezed spinach, feta, hemp, and yeast. Divide between the selected dishes so the mixture is no deeper than the original four-serving layer.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: For the original four-serving layer, bake about 25–30 minutes; for the thinner two-serving layer, begin checking at 18 minutes, until the center is set and reaches 160°F. Toss greens with the remaining oil and lemon during baking. Rest the frittata for 3 minutes before cutting into the selected number of equal adult portions.

equipment: 9-inch square metal baking dish at least 2 inches deep

Scaling: at six or eight servings use two matching 9-inch square metal dishes, dividing the mixture to preserve original depth; oven loading can increase total time. At two servings the thinner layer may finish earlier; check the center without blindly halving the timer.

recipes.title: Keto zuppa toscana
recipes.summary: Creamy Instant Pot soup with chicken Italian sausage, turkey bacon, cauliflower and kale.

ingredients.name: Chicken Italian sausage
ingredients.note: No pork; check the label for allergens and fillers.

ingredients.name: Kale
ingredients.note: Kale, not spinach.

ingredients.name: Xanthan gum
ingredients.note: Optional thickener; not counted in nutrition.

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.note: Optional garnish; not counted in nutrition.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Dice the onion, mince the garlic, chop the turkey bacon and kale, and cut cauliflower into bite-size florets. Remove sausage casings. Keep raw sausage, its board and utensils away from the kale and cream.

steps.title: Sauté
steps.text: Set the Instant Pot to Sauté. Brown the sausage, breaking it up, with the turkey bacon. Add the onion and crushed red pepper and cook until the onion softens. Add the garlic for about 30 seconds. Turn Sauté off.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the broth and scrape up browned bits so the pot does not trigger a burn warning. Add the cauliflower. Seal, switch Keep Warm off, and cook at high pressure for 5 minutes. Stay under PC MAX.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Quick release according to your manual, keeping clear of steam; vent in short bursts if the soup sputters. Open only after the float valve drops. Check the sausage reaches 165°F. Stir in the cream and kale until the kale wilts. Sprinkle in xanthan while stirring if you want a thicker soup. Serve with Parmesan if using.

timeline.attention: Brown sausage and turkey bacon, then onion, red pepper and garlic.
Deglaze with broth before sealing; Keep Warm off.
Countdown starts after pressure is reached.

tips: Deglaze thoroughly after sautéing to avoid a burn warning.

limitations: 35–45 min is a planning estimate; pressure build time varies with liquid volume and starting temperature.
Follow your exact model’s liquid minimum, PC MAX, venting and float-valve instructions. Do not leave the operating cooker unattended.
Nutrition uses USDA smoked Italian turkey sausage as the closest poultry Italian sausage profile, excluding its outlier iron value; check your sausage, bacon and broth labels.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Put potato pieces and water in a microwave-safe dish with a vented microwave-safe cover. Microwave on high for about 6–8 minutes in a roughly 1000 W microwave, until just fork-tender, then carefully uncover and drain. Prepare the rest during this step.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Before handling raw chicken, mix the oil, oregano, garlic, zest and pepper in a clean bowl. Spread potatoes over one half of a half-sheet pan, reserving the other half for beans. Set beans aside. Put unfolded chicken on the second pan. steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Roast chicken and potatoes for 20–25 minutes. Add green beans to the vegetable pan after the first 10 minutes, keeping them in a separate area rather than piling them over potatoes. Swap racks at that addition. Chicken must reach 165°F; potatoes and beans should be tender. Remove each when ready.

steps.title: Serve

recipes.title: Chicken Posole (enchilada soup)
recipes.summary: Chicken and white beans in red enchilada broth, finished with lime, cabbage and cilantro.

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper
ingredients.note: The old optional pepper is included in this estimate.

ingredients.name: Fine salt
ingredients.note: Original amount; reduce to taste if your broth or sauce is salty.

ingredients.name: Red enchilada sauce
ingredients.note: Base four-serving batch: about one 10 oz can. Estimate uses Old El Paso medium red sauce; labels vary.

ingredients.name: Cayenne pepper
ingredients.note: Original amount is very hot. Start with less if desired.

ingredients.name: Canned white beans
ingredients.note: Base four-serving batch: one 15 oz can; do not substitute dry beans.

ingredients.name: Cooked shredded chicken breast
ingredients.state: fully cooked, skinless, boneless; cooked edible weight
ingredients.note: Added in the restored version because the old Chicken Posole entry omitted a chicken amount.

ingredients.name: Cabbage
ingredients.note: Measured amount for the old to-taste garnish.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.note: Measured amount for the old to-taste garnish.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Use fully cooked shredded chicken and canned, fully cooked beans. Wash and prepare the vegetables and garnishes. Set a 4-quart or larger saucepan on the stovetop; use a larger pot or batches for six or eight servings.

steps.title: Sauté
steps.text: Heat the oil over medium heat. Cook onion and bell pepper for about 5 minutes, stirring, until softened. Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add broth, enchilada sauce, canned beans with their liquid, salt and cayenne. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer gently for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the cooked chicken and return to a simmer. Heat until chicken reaches 165°F in several places, about 5 minutes or longer as needed. Do not use raw chicken with this method.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Turn off the heat and stir in lime juice. Divide among four bowls and top with cabbage and cilantro. Taste before adding more salt or cayenne.

equipment: Stovetop and 4-quart or larger saucepan; larger pot or batches for six/eight servings

timeline.attention: Chop vegetables; soften onion and pepper, then briefly cook garlic.
Bring broth, sauce and beans to a boil; simmer 10 min, stirring occasionally.
Add fully cooked chicken, check temperature, then add lime and garnishes.

tips: The original recipe used beans, not hominy. This restores that version rather than a traditional pozole.
The source gave no pressure time. This adaptation uses a saucepan, not pressure cooking.
The original 3g cayenne is hot; use less to suit your taste.
limitations: Restored from the old Chicken Posole recipe. Its oil, onion, garlic, pepper, salt, sauce, cayenne, beans, broth and lime amounts are retained.

The source omitted chicken and a cooking time. The 400g cooked chicken and stovetop method are new; cabbage and cilantro now have measured garnish amounts. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.

Nutrition uses generic USDA ingredients, canned white beans including liquid, and an Old El Paso sauce label with an estimated 60g per quarter cup. Broth is modeled at 1g/mL. Brands, draining beans, and reducing garnishes or seasoning change the estimates.
Complete micronutrient totals are unavailable for this restored recipe and are omitted. Check chicken, broth and sauce labels for allergens.
